title: Counter Number Three
subject: A middle-aged man named Mr. Odell buys a bottle of vitamin C he does not need every Thursday at the same pharmacy counter just to hear the pharmacist, Bernadette, say hello; after eleven bottles she writes her phone number on the receipt.
caption: Stax-style Memphis horn soul, mid-tempo shuffle groove. Tight staccato baritone sax, tenor sax and trumpet horn stabs, a gritty clean-toned Telecaster playing choppy off-beat chords, a Hammond B3 organ with light Leslie swirl, a punchy melodic bass walking under a snappy snare backbeat. 1966 Memphis studio texture, tape-warm, dry room, horns tight and forward. Male lead, warm gritty tenor, mid-high register, relaxed and grinning delivery, with a small gospel-leaning backing group answering the hook. Clear full voice, every word enunciated, steady sung melody on every line. 112 BPM, Bb major. Bashful, bouncy flirtation. No trap hi-hats, no autotune, no synth pads, no EDM drops, no modern pop sheen.
lyrics:
[Intro - baritone sax and trumpet riff over Hammond and choppy guitar]

[Verse 1]
Every Thursday, half past four
Mr. Odell walks through the door
Asks for vitamin C, a bottle of ten
Third one this month and he's back again

[Pre-Chorus]
Bernadette stamps the paper bag
Says "Sir, you could stock up, you know"
He says "I like the walk, I like the line"
Looks at his shoes, he's slow to go

[Chorus]
Counter number three, counter number three
That's where my Thursday waits for me
I don't need a cure, I don't need a pill
Just one "Hello, Mr. O" and I'm well

[Verse 2]
Eleven bottles since the spring
She's kept the count of everything
Tonight she folds the receipt in two
Writes seven digits in ballpoint blue

[Pre-Chorus]
He reads it twice under the shop light hum
Walks to the door, then back he comes
Grinning wide at the counter glass
"Miss, I'll take one more of that"

[Chorus]
Counter number three, you wrote it down for me
Now Thursday's got a Friday, and a Saturday too
I don't need a cure, I don't need a pill
Just one "Hello, Mr. O" and I'm well

[Outro - horns and organ, call and response]
Thursday, Thursday, Friday's on the way
Thursday, Thursday, hey, hey, hey
